title: AI-based structure prediction doubled structural coverage of the human nuclear pore complex scaffold
summary: EMBL and Max Planck groups used AI structure prediction plus cryo-ET to build a 70-MDa model covering over 90% of the human NPC scaffold.
account: A study appeared in Science on 10 June 2022 from groups at EMBL, the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics and collaborators. They used AI-based structure prediction to model human nucleoporins and their subcomplexes. They fitted those models into cryo-electron tomographic maps of both the constricted and dilated states of the human nuclear pore complex (NPC). The authors benchmarked the predictions against previous and unpublished X-ray and cryo-EM structures and reported unprecedented accuracy. The resulting 70-MDa atomically resolved model covers more than 90% of the NPC scaffold, roughly doubling previous structural coverage. It resolves the anchoring sites of intrinsically disordered linker nucleoporins. Authors: EMBL (Heidelberg and Hamburg), the Max Planck Institute of Biophysics, Goethe University Frankfurt, the Centre for Structural Systems Biology and the University of Michigan. The readable part of the source does not name the prediction tool or its developer.
purpose: Predict protein and subcomplex structures to enable integrative modeling of a 120-MDa macromolecular machine that resisted conventional structural biology.
system: AI-based structure prediction (the source's wording; its abstract does not name the prediction tool) used within an integrative modeling pipeline
developer: Not named in the cited source, whose abstract says only 'artificial intelligence (AI)-based prediction'
deployer: EMBL Heidelberg, Max Planck Institute of Biophysics, EMBL Hamburg (Beck, Hummer, Kosinski groups)
location: Heidelberg, Frankfurt am Main and Hamburg, Germany

ratings.reason: The collaborating laboratories obtained a model that roughly doubles structural coverage of the human NPC scaffold. That is a material advance for those groups' research programs.
A 70-MDa atomically resolved model covering over 90% of the scaffold is a durable public resource for nuclear transport research. The source reports no direct patient or population benefit.

ai_role.statement: AI structure prediction generated the nucleoporin and subcomplex models that formed the input to integrative modeling. The authors state that the predictions were benchmarked against existing and new experimental structures. The resulting model was validated against earlier and new experimental data, so the AI output was independently checked rather than accepted as given.

headline: AlphaFold models cover over 90% of the human NPC scaffold
metric: covers more than 90% of the NPC scaffold, roughly doubling previous structural coverage

comparator.against: the previous structural model of the human NPC scaffold
comparator.before: 16 Nups and 35 MDa (46% of the scaffold) of the previous model
comparator.after: 25 out of ~30 Nups, and account for 70 MDa of the molecular weight of the NPC (>90% of the scaffold molecular weight)
comparator.quote: The resulting models (Fig. 1) include 25 out of ~30 Nups, and account for 70 MDa of the molecular weight of the NPC (>90% of the scaffold molecular weight) in comparison to 16 Nups and 35 MDa (46% of the scaffold) of the previous model, and largely account for the EM density observed in the constricted and dilated states.
